week.title: Anthropic to pay Akamai $11.6 billion over seven years in ...
week.summary: The warrant flips the more common pattern in circular AI deals, in which suppliers— chipmakers and cloud providers—invest directly in the AI labs that buy their products. Here, the supplier is instead...
highlights: The warrant flips the more common pattern in circular AI deals, in which suppliers— chipmakers and cloud providers—invest directly in the AI labs that buy their products. Here, the supplier is instead giving its customer a potential stake, one that grows as Anthropic’s spending with Akamai does. AMD used a similar structure with OpenAI last year, tying warrants to chip-purchase milestones. [...] The deal is the largest in Akamai’s history and continues Anthropic’s compute gobbling-streak. It also represents a bet on a less-hyped corner of AI infrastructure: CPUs. Demand for CPUs, the general-purpose chips that handle work like running code and browsing the web, has grown as AI agents take on more tasks, though Akamai didn’t say what Anthropic will use them for. [...] Anthropic is no stranger to such arrangements. Amazon, Google, Microsoft, and AMD have all invested or agreed to invest in the company while selling it chips or cloud capacity. CEO Dario Amodei told the New York Times last December that Anthropic does not participate in these deals at the “same scale as some other players.”
Akamai shares rose as much as 17% in after-hours trading on Thursday, the Wall Street Journal reported.

month.title: Anthropic to pay Akamai $11.6 billion over seven years in ...
month.summary: The warrant flips the more common pattern in circular AI deals, in which suppliers— chipmakers and cloud providers—invest directly in the AI labs that buy their products. Here, the supplier is instead...
highlights: The warrant flips the more common pattern in circular AI deals, in which suppliers— chipmakers and cloud providers—invest directly in the AI labs that buy their products. Here, the supplier is instead giving its customer a potential stake, one that grows as Anthropic’s spending with Akamai does. AMD used a similar structure with OpenAI last year, tying warrants to chip-purchase milestones. [...] The deal is the largest in Akamai’s history and continues Anthropic’s compute gobbling-streak. It also represents a bet on a less-hyped corner of AI infrastructure: CPUs. Demand for CPUs, the general-purpose chips that handle work like running code and browsing the web, has grown as AI agents take on more tasks, though Akamai didn’t say what Anthropic will use them for. [...] Anthropic is no stranger to such arrangements. Amazon, Google, Microsoft, and AMD have all invested or agreed to invest in the company while selling it chips or cloud capacity. CEO Dario Amodei told the New York Times last December that Anthropic does not participate in these deals at the “same scale as some other players.”
Akamai shares rose as much as 17% in after-hours trading on Thursday, the Wall Street Journal reported.
